page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel processor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The CPU includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8) for hardware-accelerated matrix operations.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1657.98 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1836.0. However, multi-core and memory-bound performance is limited. The stress-ng multi-core score is 1736.79, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 2242.0, both falling into weak or poor categories. Memory bandwidth is low, with large-block read speeds at 17.81 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.0 GB/sec. Database operations and software compilation also show poor performance, with Redis SET operations reaching 2.31 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 1006.28.

This server represents a low-cost entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The primary tradeoff is the low memory capacity of 4.0 GB and constrained memory bandwidth, which limits its effectiveness for data-intensive applications. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and support for advanced vector and matrix instructions, this instance is best suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, small-scale text processing, or entry-level vector math operations that fit entirely within the L3 cache of 260 MB.
